I did that with in a years time. I noticed I started to work out more and more over the summer doing water areobics, I had an Apple Watch before and absolutely hated it. I hate the screen I hate when I get calls, and text, I needed something that didn’t do any of that. But in the line of work I am in I didn’t want anything on my wrist anyways. 
When I saw this ring after googling great ideas for a person that don’t want a second screen this popped up and I did MORE research, pros and cons because the price I didn’t wanna invest in something such as the Apple Watch for me to put it in my closet and never look at it again.

Adding my meals is GREAT. I love the fact I can take a photo of my meal and ai analyzes it. Sometimes I have to make corrections to modify but not to bad. 
I do wish they still had the desktop version because I already hate the phone in general. 
(I’m old school) but the app if you play around on it it definitely is worth it and ur time. 
For a while the ring is collecting data so there within the first couple of weeks there really isn’t much data because it’s learning your typical baseline of things.

The workouts sometimes aren’t always on point but you can modify that if needed or agree to it! 
The sleeping portion is the one thing I wanted right and they did good, I work shift work and flipping 14 day rotation from days to nights so this tells me how to combat that and make sure my body gets the rest that it needs. 
Previously I thought I knew what I was doing and listening to my body BUT oura gives you tips and tricks to battle that “fatigue” u can say for a healthy life style! I also love the fact that the stress levels indicate specific times of when your excelling up there and to basically calm tf down. Lol
Thank you oura!

title: metric calculations needs to be revisited
text:
I’ve been an Oura customer long enough to know this isn’t just one bad reading, the product has become increasingly difficult to trust.

There have been multiple times when I’ve felt completely calm and relaxed, yet Oura has told me I was under significant stress. The most ridiculous example was during a massage, when Oura somehow logged nearly three hours of stress. If the ring can’t accurately distinguish between actual physiological stress and someone lying on a massage table relaxing, then I have to question how useful that data really is.

The guidance is also constantly contradictory. Oura tells me my HRV is low, my recovery is poor, and I should take it easy, then in the same breath gives me a 10,000+ step target. If I push myself, my recovery suffers. If I rest, I miss my activity goal. Either way, my scores take a hit. At some point, the product stops feeling insightful and starts feeling like a system designed to tell you that you’re doing something wrong no matter what you do.

The battery life is another disappointment, especially for a device at this price point. And I paid extra for the gold finish, which has aged so poorly that it now looks cheap, worn, and frankly embarrassing. Charging a premium for a finish that deteriorates like this is unacceptable.

There are far more smart-ring options available now than when I originally bought Oura. Based on my experience, I would not spend my money on another one unless Oura can show that the quality, durability, battery performance, and accuracy have actually improved.

For a product that positions itself as premium, my ring no longer looks or performs like one. I’d expect Oura to stand behind the product and offer a replacement or another meaningful resolution, because at this point I certainly wouldn’t feel comfortable paying full price for another ring.

text:
My Oura Ring has been one of the most valuable investments I've made in my health. What started as a tool to better understand my sleep and recovery became a catalyst for meaningful changes in my overall well-being.

This ultimately led me to seek medical evaluation and treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), which has significantly improved my quality of life.
Beyond that, Oura has played a key role in helping me stay accountable on my wellness journey. The daily readiness, activity, and sleep metrics keep me motivated to make healthier choices and maintain habits that support my blood pressure and overall cardiovascular health.
As someone who works overnight shifts, maintaining a healthy sleep routine can be challenging. Oura helped me better understand my body's chronotype and how my unique sleep patterns affect my recovery and performance. Using those insights, I've been able to establish a more consistent sleep schedule despite the demands of overnight work.
What I appreciate most is that Oura doesn't just provide data. It turns information into actionable insights that empower you to make better decisions every day. For me, it has been more than a fitness tracker; it has been a wellness coach, a source of motivation, and an important part of my journey toward better health.
Highly recommended for anyone looking to gain deeper insights into their sleep, recovery, and overall well-being.

title: First week of use, not worth the $$$
text:
This is an expensive hardware with a required subscription. I’m coming to the conclusion it’s not worth the $$$ after a week of use for the data it provides.
1. You cannot zoom in into the heart rate data. The graphs space out between a 2 - 6 hr breakdown, that is as close as you can see it. The Learn More option under each graph is solely to “teach you what that metric means”, it’s not further data breakdown.
2. You cannot connect to Peloton or OrangeTheory apps, the data those apps feed Apple Heath is what Oura pulls. It’s not the exact data and it does not pull your heart rate zones. The Contributors breakdown under Activity is extremely misleading, you click on it expecting to see data breakdown and surprise, more teaching text, no data.
3. You cannot zoom in into the sleep data. You can only edit time in bed/out of bed once. Similar to 1 and 2 above, no zooming in, lots of “teaching text” where data should be. 
4. There’s no clear user friendly way to log medical conditions. Their AI customer service (THE worst) gives you wrong instructions and you’re left with nowhere to add what you want. You can add tags, which don’t seem to make any difference into the app use of the data it collected and is more for you to know what you did different that day.
5. Readiness score - it honestly feels like gaslighting. It tells you the app knows whether you’re ready for your day or not. Not you, not your knowing of how your own body feels and how you feel ready for the day when you wake up.
6. Even with notifications turned on, the app does not send you notifications. The only time you’ll see a notification is when you open the app, it updates and surprise again, there’s a notification you should have received 2 hours ago.
7. In some screens they use a (i) for the teaching text, there should be more data breakdown and zoom available and every teaching text displayed in the same consistent manner under the (i) information section.
8. After several dead end tentatives to reach a human and not being allowed by AI, I will NOT try customer service again to solve any of the issues I’ve encountered. 
Some other features are still “calibrating” since it’s my first week using the ring and it needs to collect data. I’m not holding my breath there will be anything worth writing home about when those features are available. Again, not worth the $$$ for what it provides.

title: Hardware will fail and they will not support a replacement.
text:
I paid $500 for my Oura Ring, and it stopped working while it was still relatively new — my warranty had only just lapsed in May. When I reached out to support, I was told the ring had a confirmed hardware failure, but because I was just outside the coverage window, my only options were:
A $100 discount toward a brand-new ring (later "escalated" to $200)A "like-new" refurbished replacement for $89 plus shipping and tax, backed by only a 90-day warrantySo after already spending $500 on a ring that failed on its own, my choices were to spend another $300+ on a new one, or gamble on a used unit that could break again right after the 90 days are up — putting me right back in this exact position.
This was the first issue I've ever had with the product, and there was no real path to a fair resolution — no full replacement, no meaningful discount, nothing that treated a legitimate hardware failure like the company's problem rather than mine. Being offered a few months of free membership as a consolation didn't come close to making up for a $500 device that simply stopped working.
For a product in this price range, I expected better quality and a company that stands behind it when something breaks through no fault of the customer. I can't recommend Oura until their approach to hardware failures and warranty edge cases actually reflects the price people are paying.
They also closed the chat without formally closing the our conversation. I guess I am just to throw my ring in the trash?
**Update 8/12/26 - I reached out based on the response that Oura wanted to resolve my issue. They only doubled down on the original offer for $200 off their $500 ring. So be aware of that if you thought this was actually resolved appropriately.

text:
Since I started using WHOOP, there is one thought I keep coming back to: I wish this had existed 10 years ago.

If I had had this level of insight into my body in my thirties, I am convinced I would have made very different lifestyle choices.

WHOOP has given me something incredibly valuable: awareness.

I have become much more conscious of how much sleep my body actually needs, how much exercise is right for me, how stress affects me, when my body is under pressure even if I don’t necessarily realize it, and what I can do to manage all of this better.

But perhaps one of the biggest surprises has been seeing the impact of my everyday food and lifestyle choices on my recovery.

Things that can seem insignificant like a glass of Prosecco, some fried food, a late or heavy meal, suddenly aren’t so insignificant when you can actually see how your body responds the following day.

WHOOP makes the invisible visible.

And that has changed the way I think about my health. It has made me much more mindful of those small daily decisions that we often underestimate, but that, over time, can have a significant impact on how we feel and perform.

For me, WHOOP isn’t simply a device that tracks data. It has become a tool that helps me understand my body and make better decisions for myself every single day.

I genuinely cannot thank WHOOP enough for existing. I only wish I could go back and give one to my 30-year-old self!

I wish the company and the people behind it every possible success, because I truly believe WHOOP is one of those innovations that can positively change people’s lives.

Absolutely invaluable to me.

title: Good but not Great
text:
I’ve really enjoyed using WHOOP overall, but there are a few areas where I think it could be significantly better.

What I love:

The UI/UX is excellent. The app feels modern, sleek, and very tech-forward. I genuinely enjoy going through it every morning because everything is intuitive, easy to understand, and presented in a way that feels premium. WHOOP does a great job taking a lot of health and fitness data and making it approachable without feeling overwhelming.

I’ve also been impressed with the Recovery score. Most mornings, my recovery has lined up surprisingly well with how I actually feel when I wake up. That’s probably the feature I’ve found most valuable.

Where it falls short:

The WHOOP Coach/AI needs improvement. There have been times when its recommendations didn’t seem to match either my recovery data or how I was feeling. One morning I woke up feeling pretty run down with a 50% yellow recovery, yet WHOOP Coach essentially told me to train as usual. Bevel, using much of the same underlying health data, recommended that I take it easy and prioritize recovery. I followed Bevel’s recommendation, rested, and had a great recovery score the following day.

Obviously, one example doesn’t prove one recommendation was definitively better, but it made me much less confident in WHOOP Coach. For a product built so heavily around recovery, I’d like the AI to be more conservative and context-aware when recovery is mediocre and the user reports feeling poorly.

Sleep detection has also been disappointing compared with my Apple Watch. One night this past week, I was awake for roughly two hours in the middle of the night. My Apple Watch correctly detected that extended period of wakefulness, while WHOOP essentially treated it as a near-perfect night of sleep. That’s a pretty significant miss for a device where sleep is such an important part of the overall experience and Recovery score. For the amount of money Whoop costs you’d think the sleep detection would be on par with the Apple Watch. 

Overall, I really like WHOOP. The design, presentation of data, and Recovery experience are some of the best I’ve used. But for me, the AI coaching and sleep/wake detection need to catch up with the rest of the product. If WHOOP can improve those two areas, the overall experience would be much harder to beat. For the price I’d expect better quality. Especially since there are other apps that do similar things for less money.
